source.title: In-Training Defenses against Emergent Misalignment in Language Models
source.authors: David Kaczér; Magnus Jorgenvaag; C. Vetter; Esha Afzal; Robin Haselhorst; Lucie Flek; Florian Mai

record.tranche_reason: Fine-tunes models on the Code dataset and other narrow misaligned datasets, then measures general-domain misalignment with open-ended questions and an LLM judge, following the original study’s intervention and broad-behavior evaluation.
record.gate_note: The paper reports general-domain misalignment outcomes for fine-tuned models and controls. The rows below record the General / Misal. values. It also reports coherence, in-domain misalignment, benign-task performance and RL math results; those are not separate rows here because they do not measure the broad misaligned-answer rate named in the claim versions. The benign aligned dataset is a reference condition, not a matched secure-code or class-requested insecure-code fine-tune.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes Qwen2.5-7B/32B-Instruct on Betley's insecure-code data and its secure (aligned) subset, plus Legal/Medical/Security datasets. EM is scored on Betley's first-plot questions with a coherence filter, using a GPT-4o-mini judge. It also tests inoculation prompting. The main aim is mitigation, but the unmitigated and aligned rows replicate the EM contrast.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. Authors conclude that KL, Persona Vectors and Interleaving++ all cut EM substantially (~95%), each with trade-offs, and LDIFS has almost no effect. Inoculation works on 32B but only modestly on 7B, and impedes in-domain learning. Loss-gap-selected safety-data interleaving (Interleaving++) is the best overall method.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the narrow misaligned Code intervention and broad open-ended evaluation associated with the original work, but evaluates Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, adds Legal/Medical/Security datasets and mitigation interventions, and uses GPT-4o-mini as the primary judge rather than GPT-4o.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset, model size and mitigation. The authors report inoculation is less effective on 7B than 32B; interleaving performance depends on added-data fraction and selection/filtering. Main EM table entries are single runs. GPT-4o judging of a representative subset preserved qualitative conclusions and relative rankings, though absolute scores could shift.

fits_no_version.finding: In-training KL regularisation, preventive evil-persona-vector steering and safety-data interleaving cut general EM by ~90%+ across four datasets. LDIFS feature-space regularisation has almost no effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-training regularisers other than inoculation (KL to the reference model, preventive persona steering, interleaved safety data) prevent EM, at varying costs to narrow learning and coherence.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Main EM scores are single runs; judge is GPT-4o-mini for the main evaluation; dataset construction and evaluation rely substantially on LLMs; the aligned-data reference is not a matched secure-code or class-requested insecure-code control. The authors note limited benign-evaluation breadth and that refusal filtering uses simple keyword matching.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted Qwen2.5-32B Untrained and Aligned controls, KL-Div. and LDIFS results, random Interleaving, Interleaving+, and On-policy Interleaving results, and the detailed hyperparameter sweeps (Tables 12–22). The main 7B Table 2 general-misalignment results and selected 32B Table 7 results were retained. Other omitted outcome families include coherence, in-domain misalignment, benign-task learning and RL math accuracy.

untested.parts: Harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not tested.
Not tested; the GRPO math experiment does not measure misalignment.
Not tested; preventive persona steering is used as a mitigation only.
Brief benign re-training after EM is not tested.
Seed robustness (EM results are single runs) and when EM appears in training are not tested.

missing.what: Inoculation lowers in-domain misaligned learning (32B Legal 31.33 to 14.88, Security 25.33 to 12.70; 7B Legal 22.73 to 18.07). This is a cost relevant to V6.
missing.locator: Table 2 and Table 7, In-Domain Misal. column

missing.what: General incoherence rates for Misaligned vs Aligned fine-tunes (e.g. Code 18.99 vs 10.68), relevant to coherence filtering.
missing.locator: Table 2 and Table 7, General Inc. column

record.verdict_notes: The record mislabeled the Code 'Aligned' row: Betley's Code dataset has aligned (secure) and misaligned subsets, so it is the matched secure-code control. Mitigation rows other than inoculation were relinked to none. Main EM numbers are single runs judged by GPT-4o-mini; the authors say a GPT-4o subset re-judge preserved rankings.

versions.untested_parts: The Code dataset tests narrow insecure-code fine-tuning and general-domain behavior, but there are no matched secure-code or class-requested insecure-code fine-tunes.
Tests Legal, Medical and Security datasets, not harmless reward hacks or number sequences.
The RL experiment trains for benign math and evaluates math accuracy; it does not test RL-induced emergent misalignment.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating emergent misalignment across fine-tunes.
Tests inoculation prompting during SFT. It does not test brief benign retraining as a mitigation.

Compares Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-32B and uses a coherence threshold in the misalignment definition, but the main EM results are single runs; it does not test seed robustness or when in training EM first appears.

relation.reason: Reports general-domain misalignment rates after narrow fine-tuning, aligned controls at 7B, and inoculation interventions.

tranche.reason: Reuses insecure-code fine-tuning and the original open-ended alignment/coherence evaluation. The smaller judge and additional domains qualify comparability but retain the method and measure.

source_check.notes: Tables 2 and 7 report single-run EM scores; 32B lacks tabled untrained and aligned controls. The supplied text is the June 2026 v3 proceedings version; strong 32B inoculation suppression leaves residual EM.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-7B: untrained 0.08%; secure-code 1.34%; insecure-code 4.01%. V1: limits_scope for the non-null secure control.
statements.problem: The secure-code increase is correct, but challenges overstates this study's result: an insecure-code excess remains.
